purpose: Preserve one semantic object identity across six appearances without sharing era artwork, geometry, material, perspective, or size hints.
continuityRules: Runtime ids, product names, actions, and state meanings stay stable across appearances.
Historical system objects use the target operating system's real prototype before custom product objects are drawn.
Custom objects keep one physical metaphor across eras only when that metaphor remains period-plausible.
Every appearance owns independent large and small artwork; no appearance is recolored, flattened, thresholded, or glass-wrapped from another.
Selection, dragging, disabled state, and Finder label treatment belong to the system surface rather than the icon artwork.

finderApp.continuity: The friendly operating environment: a compact Macintosh whose screen carries two eyes and a small smile. Every era redraws the hardware, material, perspective, and pixel hints independently; the face and compact-computer silhouette stay recognizable.
finderApp.productBasis: Finder is the user's friendly system identity. The browser-window metaphor belongs to the Finder window itself, not to the application icon.

multiFinderApp.continuity: Exactly two overlapping friendly compact Macintosh Finder identities. Both smiling screens remain recognizable while every era redraws the cases, material, perspective, overlap, and small-size hints independently.
multiFinderApp.productBasis: MultiFinder adds concurrent application environments while retaining Finder identity; the pair expresses multiplicity without becoming two generic windows or tabs.

folder.continuity: A system-owned container; reproduce the target era's real Finder folder.

hardDisk.continuity: A mounted local storage volume; reproduce the target era's real disk prototype.

trash.continuity: The system waste container; empty and full are states of the same object.

document.continuity: A neutral editable paper or document owned by the target system.

daHandler.continuity: The target era's generic application or utility container, not an AI logo.

fileFloppy.continuity: Temporary removable context media; literal floppy where period-correct, translated to era-appropriate removable media later.

projectDisk.continuity: Durable project storage: a period-correct volume with one restrained project label cue.

searcher.continuity: A single magnifying glass; material, perspective, and optical construction change per era.

teachText.continuity: A writing document with a period-correct writing instrument or text-editor identity.

scrapbook.continuity: A bound album holding selected clippings; never a generic notes page.

assistant.continuity: Two speech balloons: the user's turn has a solid outline and the model reply has a clearly dashed outline. The dash is semantic, not decoration: model output remains provisional until the user saves, clips, inserts, or exports it.
assistant.productBasis: The icon exposes the product's temporary-output rule at the point of recognition. It is distinct from rounded message bubbles inside the ClioTalk window, which remain outside the historical window grammar.

controlPanel.continuity: The target era's real Control Panel, System Preferences, or Settings prototype.

reviewDesk.continuity: A document under proofing or correction, reduced to one readable compound object.

docMap.continuity: The document's own structure drawn as a branching map: a page whose headings grow into a stem and branches. It is not a geographic map and not a modern node graph; the branches are the document's headings, which is what the tool actually renders.
docMap.productBasis: DocMap renders a Markdown document's heading structure as a mind map with tree, radial, and fishbone layouts, one-sided or symmetric, generated from a selection or a whole source.

projectDisc.continuity: Finished export media, represented by the target era's optical or archival medium.

systemFile.continuity: The target era's native system software container or identity object.

clipboard.continuity: A period-correct clipboard for transient copied material; distinct from Scrapbook's durable selected clippings.

multiFinderApp.chronology: MultiFinder is later than System 6 Finder evidence. The Classic artwork is an explicitly documented period approximation, not a native System 6 resource claim.

metaphorKeyRule: Objects with a metaphorKey keep that one physical metaphor in every appearance; each appearance still owns independent artwork, geometry, material, and size-specific hints. Objects without a key are system objects and follow the target operating system's own prototype instead.

historicalValidation.purpose: Record what actually validated each appearance. An accepted review status means a human looked at the artwork and kept it; it is not a claim that the artwork was checked against a period Macintosh. Only the evidence classes below carry that claim.

evidenceClasses.native-resource: Measured against the real resource fork or Apple .iconset held in internal/evidence. Historical claim allowed.
evidenceClasses.period-capture: Measured against a captured screenshot of the running system held in internal/evidence. Historical claim allowed for silhouette, hue, perspective and visual weight.
evidenceClasses.accepted-generated: Painted by a checked-in generator and kept after human review. NOT historical validation.
evidenceClasses.accepted-imagegen: Drawn by Image Gen against reference material and kept after human review. NOT historical validation.

classic.note: Runtime artwork is a smooth Retina SVG reconstruction of the native silhouette, not a bitmap copy. The remaining objects are product stand-ins with no native prototype.

platinum.source: internal/evidence/drafts/theme-lab-fidelity-cache/platinum (Mac OS 9.0 Finder, desktop and file manager captures)
platinum.note: The capture shows front-facing folders with a hard offset shadow. The shipped folder is a rotated three-quarter view and does not match.

aqua.note: The whole 56-object family is generator output. The captured Apple artwork disagrees on folder perspective, disk and trash hue, document content, and the generic application object.

snow-leopard.note: The whole 56-object family is generator output. Apple's own .iconset disagrees on folder value and perspective, document colour and content, and the generic application object.

yosemite.note: The whole 56-object family is generator output. The folder matches the capture; the generic document carries a solid colour block the real system does not have.

liquid-glass.note: No period Macintosh exists to measure against yet. The generic document has almost no contrast against a light desktop, and the trash reads as a drinking glass rather than a bin.

knownIdentityConflicts.conflict: The ledger keeps one smiling compact Macintosh across all six appearances. Mac OS X 10.0 onward ships a two-tone blue Finder face instead, so the four OS X appearances follow product continuity rather than the real prototype.
knownIdentityConflicts.decision: Held on purpose. Changing it would break the strongest row in the system; it is recorded here so it is never mistaken for an oversight.

knownIdentityConflicts.conflict: The anchor asks for the target era's generic application container. Aqua, Snow Leopard and Yosemite draw a window instead of Apple's pencil-ruler-brush generic application.
knownIdentityConflicts.decision: Open. Listed in the regeneration brief.

knownIdentityConflicts.conflict: The object is a stack of paper in System 6 and Mac OS 9, a bound book in Aqua, Snow Leopard and Yosemite, and a page again in Tahoe. The book form also collides with reader.
knownIdentityConflicts.decision: Open. Listed in the regeneration brief.
